Motorola Boosts Counter-Drone Security Footprint With D-Fend Buyout
Fri, October 2, 2026 at 6:00 AM PDT 3 min read
Motorola Solutions, Inc. MSI has augmented its presence in the rapidly expanding counter-drone security market with the acquisition of D-Fend Solutions. The transaction adds D-Fend's field-proven counter-unmanned aerial systems (C-UAS) technology to Motorola's broader mission-critical safety and security ecosystem.
The $1.5-billion deal appears to be the call of the hour as unauthorized drones increasingly pose security risks to airports, stadiums, critical infrastructure, military installations and densely populated areas. In addition to securing another fast-growing business, D-Fend expands Motorola's addressable market, enabling it to leverage extensive public-safety customer relationships to accelerate adoption of counter-drone technology.
D-Fend Strengthens Counter-Drone Capabilities
The D-Fend acquisition is expected to strengthen Motorola's presence in the fast-growing counter-drone market. D-Fend's EnforceAir platform differentiates itself from conventional systems that typically rely on jamming or kinetic interception, which can disrupt nearby communications or pose collateral risks.
EnforceAir uses radio-frequency cyber-takeover technology to detect and assume control of unauthorized drones and safely redirect them to a designated landing area. Importantly, the platform can neutralize rogue drones without affecting authorized drone operations or surrounding communications infrastructure. This makes the solution well suited for sensitive environments such as airports, large public events, urban areas and other locations where jamming or kinetic methods may be less practical.
Acquisition Bolsters Broader Drone Strategy
The buyout also complements Motorola's expanding presence across the unmanned-systems ecosystem. Through Silvus Technologies, the company already offers resilient wireless networking solutions used in defense applications, including unmanned platforms. Its partnership with BRINC further provides public-safety agencies with drones-as-first-responders capabilities, enabling aerial situational awareness and real-time video transmission to command centers.
The addition of D-Fend broadens Motorola's exposure across defense-focused unmanned communications, public-safety drone applications and counter-drone solutions. Moreover, the company's established relationships with federal agencies, state and local public-safety organizations and enterprise customers could provide a ready distribution channel for D-Fend's offerings.
Management noted that Motorola has worked with D-Fend for several years and jointly pursued opportunities with federal law-enforcement agencies prior to the transaction. The combination of complementary technologies and an established customer network could support D-Fend's growth without requiring Motorola to build a separate go-to-market infrastructure.
Despite the $1.5-billion purchase price and related financing costs, management expects the transaction to be modestly accretive to earnings in 2027. D-Fend's existing profitability, healthy growth trajectory and expanding addressable market are likely to support the expected contribution.
The buyout could eventually produce a more comprehensive air-to-ground security platform, offering a product breadth that may become increasingly important as public-safety customers look to consolidate security workflows rather than deploy isolated point solutions. It could further help Motorola better compete with rivals such as Ondas Inc. ONDS, Unusual Machines, Inc. UMAC and Draganfly Inc. DPRO.

Covilhã-based AI video analytics company to be integrated into Motorola Solutions' Avigilon platform
MAMARONECK, N.Y., Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Young America Capital, LLC ("YAC") today announced that it advised DeepNeuronic, a Portuguese developer of AI video analytics, on its sale to Motorola Solutions, Inc. (NYSE: MSI). Motorola Solutions acquired 100% of DeepNeuronic's share capital, including its Brazilian subsidiary. Terms were not disclosed.
DeepNeuronic was founded in 2021 by Vasco Lopes and Bruno Degardin, who met at Portugal's University of Beira Interior and earned their PhDs there in artificial intelligence and computer vision. Their software reads live camera feeds and flags incidents as they happen. Highway operators, airports, manufacturers and retailers in Portugal and Brazil already run it on the cameras they have. Motorola Solutions will build the technology into Avigilon, its video security platform, which serves customers in more than 100 countries. DeepNeuronic's 17-person team is joining Motorola Solutions and will stay in Covilhã.
"This was one of the sharper deals we worked on this year," said Peter Formanek, Founder and CEO of YAC. "Vasco and Bruno had a product customers were already paying for and a clear view of where video analytics was going. Motorola Solutions saw it too. Our job was to get both sides to a deal that worked, across two continents and a lot of time zones, and Ran did exactly that."
Ran Zfoni, Vice President and Head of Israel & Europe Tech at YAC, advised DeepNeuronic's founders through the transaction. Cuatrecasas served as legal counsel to DeepNeuronic, with a team led by partner Vasco Bivar de Azevedo.
"The founders knew what they wanted: a buyer that could scale the technology and would keep the team together in Covilhã," said Zfoni. "Motorola Solutions was that buyer. Congratulations to Vasco, Bruno and everyone at DeepNeuronic."

Motorolans on a Mission: Serving the Community From the Office to the Front Lines
NORTHAMPTON, MA / ACCESS Newswire / September 29, 2026 / While most people use their vacation to disconnect, U.K.-based Motorola Solutions employee Mike Beddoes dedicates his time to answering a higher call, stepping up to the front lines to protect his community.
For nine years, Mike has balanced a dual purpose: driving innovation at Motorola Solutions by day and serving as a fully warranted volunteer officer with the Warwickshire Police Special Constabulary by night. His dedication recently went a step further, as he committed four weeks of his personal time off to complete a rigorous emergency driving course.
As a "Special Constable," Mike wears the same uniform and holds the same authority as a full-time officer. He has logged more than 3,000 hours of service, the equivalent of two full years of police work. His commitment began on his university commute where he watched officers meet chaos with calm. Seeing them guide people through their darkest moments inspired him to move past watching and start helping.
Mike's service ranges from routine patrols to critical, life-or-death interventions. Notably, he recently earned his fourth Chief Constable Commendation after stepping into a major house fire while off-duty. Without hesitation, he ran toward the danger, administered first aid to those trapped inside and helped contain the blaze.
In recognition of his 3,000 hours of service and recent act of bravery, Mike was honored with the 2025 CEO Award for Volunteerism, Motorola Solutions' highest award for service.
"Receiving this type of recognition is an incredible honor," said Mike. "But the real reward is the impact we get to make on the ground. When you're responding to an emergency or stepping into a critical situation, you aren't thinking about the hours or the personal time off you gave up - you're just focusing on the person who needs your help. I'm grateful to be in a position to protect and serve the community I live in."
Mike serves as a vital bridge between the technologies Motorola Solutions delivers and the first responders who rely on them. His front-line experience gives him a uniquely powerful perspective. When Mike holds a radio in the middle of an emergency, he knows exactly what's at stake. He understands firsthand that a clear signal and a reliable device are more than convenient features - they're critical lifelines. Mike brings this profound connection to our purpose back to his daily work at Motorola Solutions, inspiring his team to build with the end-user in mind.
Mike's journey is a powerful reminder that our impact extends beyond our technology. It's measured in the lives we touch and the communities we help keep safe. He stands alongside Motorolans around the world who embody this same spirit and a shared dedication to serve.

On September 9, Motorola Solutions, Inc. (NYSE:MSI) announced that its Board of Directors approved a $2 billion expansion to its share repurchase program, raising the company's cumulative repurchase authorization since July 2011 to $20 billion. The updated program has no fixed expiration date and builds on the company's previously authorized $18 billion buyback plan, which had approximately $0.6 billion in remaining capacity at the end of Q2 2026. Under the program, management retains flexibility to repurchase shares periodically through open-market or privately negotiated transactions based on prevailing market conditions.

Capital Authorization Directly Supported by Cash Flow
For Motorola Solutions, Inc. (NYSE:MSI), expanding share repurchase capacity reinforces management's confidence in the company's long-term earnings trajectory and cash generation capability. In Q2 2026, the company generated $469 million in operating cash flow, up $197 million year-over-year, and $414 million in free cash flow. Multi-year revenue visibility is further underpinned by a record ending backlog of $15.6 billion (up 11%), providing a predictable multi-quarter revenue foundation that reduces reliance on short-term procurement cycles.

While buybacks enhance per-share metrics, dedicating capital to share repurchases presents strategic trade-offs given the company's leverage profile and capital requirements. A debt-heavy balance sheet increases sensitivity to interest expenses and macroeconomic shifts, making large capital returns dependent on uninterrupted cash flow generation.

Higher memory and component costs are projected to weigh on second-half gross margins, requiring sustained productivity gains. At the same time, Motorola Solutions, Inc. Motorola Boosts Counter-Drone Security Footprint With D-Fend Buyout
Fri, October 2, 2026 at 6:00 AM PDT 3 min read
Motorola Solutions, Inc. MSI has augmented its presence in the rapidly expanding counter-drone security market with the acquisition of D-Fend Solutions. The transaction adds D-Fend's field-proven counter-unmanned aerial systems (C-UAS) technology to Motorola's broader mission-critical safety and security ecosystem.
The $1.5-billion deal appears to be the call of the hour as unauthorized drones increasingly pose security risks to airports, stadiums, critical infrastructure, military installations and densely populated areas. In addition to securing another fast-growing business, D-Fend expands Motorola's addressable market, enabling it to leverage extensive public-safety customer relationships to accelerate adoption of counter-drone technology.
D-Fend Strengthens Counter-Drone Capabilities
The D-Fend acquisition is expected to strengthen Motorola's presence in the fast-growing counter-drone market. D-Fend's EnforceAir platform differentiates itself from conventional systems that typically rely on jamming or kinetic interception, which can disrupt nearby communications or pose collateral risks.
EnforceAir uses radio-frequency cyber-takeover technology to detect and assume control of unauthorized drones and safely redirect them to a designated landing area. Importantly, the platform can neutralize rogue drones without affecting authorized drone operations or surrounding communications infrastructure. This makes the solution well suited for sensitive environments such as airports, large public events, urban areas and other locations where jamming or kinetic methods may be less practical.
Acquisition Bolsters Broader Drone Strategy
The buyout also complements Motorola's expanding presence across the unmanned-systems ecosystem. Through Silvus Technologies, the company already offers resilient wireless networking solutions used in defense applications, including unmanned platforms. Its partnership with BRINC further provides public-safety agencies with drones-as-first-responders capabilities, enabling aerial situational awareness and real-time video transmission to command centers.
The addition of D-Fend broadens Motorola's exposure across defense-focused unmanned communications, public-safety drone applications and counter-drone solutions. Moreover, the company's established relationships with federal agencies, state and local public-safety organizations and enterprise customers could provide a ready distribution channel for D-Fend's offerings.
Management noted that Motorola has worked with D-Fend for several years and jointly pursued opportunities with federal law-enforcement agencies prior to the transaction. The combination of complementary technologies and an established customer network could support D-Fend's growth without requiring Motorola to build a separate go-to-market infrastructure.
Despite the $1.5-billion purchase price and related financing costs, management expects the transaction to be modestly accretive to earnings in 2027. D-Fend's existing profitability, healthy growth trajectory and expanding addressable market are likely to support the expected contribution.
The buyout could eventually produce a more comprehensive air-to-ground security platform, offering a product breadth that may become increasingly important as public-safety customers look to consolidate security workflows rather than deploy isolated point solutions. It could further help Motorola better compete with rivals such as Ondas Inc. ONDS, Unusual Machines, Inc. UMAC and Draganfly Inc. DPRO.

Young America Capital Advises DeepNeuronic on Sale to Motorola Solutions
Covilhã-based AI video analytics company to be integrated into Motorola Solutions' Avigilon platform
MAMARONECK, N.Y., Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Young America Capital, LLC ("YAC") today announced that it advised DeepNeuronic, a Portuguese developer of AI video analytics, on its sale to Motorola Solutions, Inc. (NYSE: MSI). Motorola Solutions acquired 100% of DeepNeuronic's share capital, including its Brazilian subsidiary. Terms were not disclosed.
DeepNeuronic was founded in 2021 by Vasco Lopes and Bruno Degardin, who met at Portugal's University of Beira Interior and earned their PhDs there in artificial intelligence and computer vision. Their software reads live camera feeds and flags incidents as they happen. Highway operators, airports, manufacturers and retailers in Portugal and Brazil already run it on the cameras they have. Motorola Solutions will build the technology into Avigilon, its video security platform, which serves customers in more than 100 countries. DeepNeuronic's 17-person team is joining Motorola Solutions and will stay in Covilhã.
"This was one of the sharper deals we worked on this year," said Peter Formanek, Founder and CEO of YAC. "Vasco and Bruno had a product customers were already paying for and a clear view of where video analytics was going. Motorola Solutions saw it too. Our job was to get both sides to a deal that worked, across two continents and a lot of time zones, and Ran did exactly that."
Ran Zfoni, Vice President and Head of Israel & Europe Tech at YAC, advised DeepNeuronic's founders through the transaction. Cuatrecasas served as legal counsel to DeepNeuronic, with a team led by partner Vasco Bivar de Azevedo.
"The founders knew what they wanted: a buyer that could scale the technology and would keep the team together in Covilhã," said Zfoni. "Motorola Solutions was that buyer. Congratulations to Vasco, Bruno and everyone at DeepNeuronic."
Young America Capital, LLC is an investment bank based in Mamaroneck, New York. YAC advises founders and owners of lower-middle-market companies in the U.S. and abroad on M&A, capital raising and strategic transactions. Member FINRA/SIPC. www.yacapital.com

Motorolans on a Mission: Serving the Community From the Office to the Front Lines
NORTHAMPTON, MA / ACCESS Newswire / September 29, 2026 / While most people use their vacation to disconnect, U.K.-based Motorola Solutions employee Mike Beddoes dedicates his time to answering a higher call, stepping up to the front lines to protect his community.
For nine years, Mike has balanced a dual purpose: driving innovation at Motorola Solutions by day and serving as a fully warranted volunteer officer with the Warwickshire Police Special Constabulary by night. His dedication recently went a step further, as he committed four weeks of his personal time off to complete a rigorous emergency driving course.
As a "Special Constable," Mike wears the same uniform and holds the same authority as a full-time officer. He has logged more than 3,000 hours of service, the equivalent of two full years of police work. His commitment began on his university commute where he watched officers meet chaos with calm. Seeing them guide people through their darkest moments inspired him to move past watching and start helping.
Mike's service ranges from routine patrols to critical, life-or-death interventions. Notably, he recently earned his fourth Chief Constable Commendation after stepping into a major house fire while off-duty. Without hesitation, he ran toward the danger, administered first aid to those trapped inside and helped contain the blaze.
In recognition of his 3,000 hours of service and recent act of bravery, Mike was honored with the 2025 CEO Award for Volunteerism, Motorola Solutions' highest award for service.
"Receiving this type of recognition is an incredible honor," said Mike. "But the real reward is the impact we get to make on the ground. When you're responding to an emergency or stepping into a critical situation, you aren't thinking about the hours or the personal time off you gave up - you're just focusing on the person who needs your help. I'm grateful to be in a position to protect and serve the community I live in."
Mike serves as a vital bridge between the technologies Motorola Solutions delivers and the first responders who rely on them. His front-line experience gives him a uniquely powerful perspective. When Mike holds a radio in the middle of an emergency, he knows exactly what's at stake. He understands firsthand that a clear signal and a reliable device are more than convenient features - they're critical lifelines. Mike brings this profound connection to our purpose back to his daily work at Motorola Solutions, inspiring his team to build with the end-user in mind.
Mike's journey is a powerful reminder that our impact extends beyond our technology. It's measured in the lives we touch and the communities we help keep safe. He stands alongside Motorolans around the world who embody this same spirit and a shared dedication to serve.

Motorola (MSI) Has Cash to Deploy. Where Can it Create the Most Value?
On September 9, Motorola Solutions, Inc. (NYSE:MSI) announced that its Board of Directors approved a $2 billion expansion to its share repurchase program, raising the company's cumulative repurchase authorization since July 2011 to $20 billion. The updated program has no fixed expiration date and builds on the company's previously authorized $18 billion buyback plan, which had approximately $0.6 billion in remaining capacity at the end of Q2 2026. Under the program, management retains flexibility to repurchase shares periodically through open-market or privately negotiated transactions based on prevailing market conditions.
You Might Also Want To Read: Apple (AAPL) Took a Different Pricing Approach with its New iPhones in China
Motorola Solutions, Inc. (MSI) Has Cash to Put to Work. Where Could It Create the Most Value?
Capital Authorization Directly Supported by Cash Flow
For Motorola Solutions, Inc. (NYSE:MSI), expanding share repurchase capacity reinforces management's confidence in the company's long-term earnings trajectory and cash generation capability. In Q2 2026, the company generated $469 million in operating cash flow, up $197 million year-over-year, and $414 million in free cash flow. High cash conversion of reported profitability provides the necessary liquidity to execute open-market repurchases without compromising operational liquidity or dividend payments.
Furthermore, broad-based operational strength supports ongoing capital allocation. Q2 2026 revenue rose 13% year-over-year to $3.1 billion, driven by 15% growth in Products and Systems Integration ($1.91 billion) and 10% growth in Software and Services ($1.23 billion). Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 330 basis points to 32.9%, while non-GAAP EPS grew 24% to $4.41. Multi-year revenue visibility is further underpinned by a record ending backlog of $15.6 billion (up 11%), providing a predictable multi-quarter revenue foundation that reduces reliance on short-term procurement cycles.
Capital Allocation Trade-offs and Balance Sheet Risks
While buybacks enhance per-share metrics, dedicating capital to share repurchases presents strategic trade-offs given the company's leverage profile and capital requirements. A debt-heavy balance sheet increases sensitivity to interest expenses and macroeconomic shifts, making large capital returns dependent on uninterrupted cash flow generation.
Additionally, capital directed toward share buybacks must compete with near-term operational cost pressures and strategic acquisitions. Higher memory and component costs are projected to weigh on second-half gross margins, requiring sustained productivity gains. At the same time, Motorola Solutions, Inc. (NYSE:MSI) agreed to acquire counter-drone technology firm D-Fend Solutions for $1.5 billion in Q2 2026, introducing integration expenses that could temporarily pressure profitability and management capacity while combining operations.

The $2 billion increase in share buyback authorization reflects a shareholder-friendly strategy backed by strong Q2 2026 cash flow and record contract backlog. However, investors must evaluate whether aggressive stock repurchases remain the most efficient use of capital relative to debt reduction, managing elevated component cost headwinds, and successfully integrating new acquisitions like D-Fend Solutions.

Motorola Solutions stock (ISIN US6200763075) is benefiting from a strong fundamental backdrop, with first-quarter 2026 sales of USD 2.7 billion up 7% year on year and a raised full-year outlook that continues to support the high share price levels seen in recent trading as of early September 2026.Tormere research For investors, the combination of double-digit growth in key segments and record orders has become the main argument behind the current valuation.
Q1 2026 figures underpin Motorola Solutions stock
According to a filing summarizing Motorola Solutions' first-quarter 2026 results, the company generated sales of USD 2.7 billion in Q1 2026, representing a 7% increase compared with the same quarter of the prior year.Tormere research Within that total, Software and Services revenue climbed 18% year on year, while Products and Systems Integration sales rose by 1%, highlighting a clear mix shift toward recurring and higher-margin software offerings in the current reporting period.Tormere research The company reported GAAP earnings per share of USD 2.18 for Q1 2026, and on the back of record first-quarter orders and backlog, management raised its full-year 2026 revenue and earnings outlook, signaling confidence that the momentum can be sustained over the rest of the year.Tormere research
These Q1 2026 results follow a record fourth quarter and full-year 2025, when Motorola Solutions achieved its highest ever annual revenue, earnings, cash flow and ending backlog, providing a historical reference point for the current trajectory.Tormere research In the fourth quarter of 2025, sales reached USD 3.4 billion, up 12% versus the prior-year quarter, while full-year 2025 revenue grew by 8%, underscoring how the 7% year-on-year increase in Q1 2026 builds on already strong growth rather than starting from a low base.Tormere research For investors assessing Motorola Solutions stock, this quantified comparison between the record 2025 figures and the continued growth into 2026 helps frame the sustainability of the story.
Upcoming Truist technology symposium adds event focus
A fresh catalyst on the calendar is an appearance by Motorola Solutions' Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer Jack Molloy at the Truist Technology Symposium: AI Transformation & Evolving Enterprise Debates on September 15, 2026, at 2:50 p.m. Eastern Time.Investing.com According to the press release cited by Investing.com, the executive is scheduled to discuss how artificial intelligence and evolving enterprise architectures are shaping technology investment, providing another opportunity for the company to communicate its strategy to institutional investors and analysts. While such conference appearances do not typically move the share price on their own, they can reinforce existing perceptions of Motorola Solutions as a beneficiary of long-term digitalization trends in public safety, enterprise communications and command center software, which in turn relate back to the strong Software and Services growth seen in Q1 2026.
At the same time, insider activity offers a nuanced counterpoint to the bullish narrative. Recent SEC-related transaction data compiled in the same research source shows that on September 2, 2026, Motorola Solutions Chairman and CEO Gregory Q. Brown sold roughly 14,200 shares at an average price of about USD 485.22, a transaction valued at approximately USD 6.90 million, leaving him with about 66,600 shares thereafter.Tormere research Earlier in August 2026, several other senior executives and directors also disposed of smaller share blocks at prices around USD 470 to USD 477 per share, suggesting that management is taking some profits at the current valuation even as operating performance remains robust.Tormere research For investors, such insider selling is not necessarily a bearish signal on its own, but it does introduce a tangible risk factor alongside the otherwise positive earnings trajectory.
Public safety and mission-critical communications remain core
Motorola Solutions is best known for its mission-critical communications and public safety solutions, including land mobile radio systems and integrated command center software used by police, fire and emergency services around the world. A representative product is the company's portfolio of APX series public safety radios, which are designed to provide reliable, encrypted voice communications for first responders and are often sold as part of larger systems that include dispatch consoles, network infrastructure and software platforms for incident management. In recent years, the company has increasingly emphasized cloud-connected command center software and video security solutions as growth drivers, which aligns with the 18% year-on-year increase in Software and Services revenue reported in Q1 2026.Tormere research For stock market investors, the continued shift from hardware-centric projects toward recurring software and services revenue is a central part of the investment case, as it can support higher margins and more predictable cash flows over time.
Stock valuation supported by earnings, but insider sales and execution are risks
From an investor perspective, the key takeaway is that Motorola Solutions entered 2026 on the back of record full-year 2025 results and then delivered further growth in Q1 2026, including a 7% increase in total sales, an 18% rise in Software and Services revenue and a raised full-year outlook.Tormere research This combination of strong reported figures and positive guidance provides a clear fundamental justification for the elevated share price levels reflected in the insider transactions during August and early September 2026, where senior executives sold shares in the USD 470 to USD 485 price range.Tormere research However, the fact that multiple insiders chose to reduce their holdings at these levels underlines that valuation risk is present: if growth were to slow or if public safety budgets were pressured, the premium currently attached to Motorola Solutions stock could come under scrutiny.
Looking ahead, the next visible event is the Truist Technology Symposium session on September 15, 2026, where the company's Chief Operating Officer is expected to discuss AI transformation and enterprise technology debates.Investing.com While this is not an earnings release, such appearances can provide incremental insight into management's priorities around artificial intelligence, cloud software and integrated solutions, which are central themes for sustaining double-digit Software and Services growth beyond Q1 2026.Tormere research Investors will also be watching for the next formal quarterly report in Motorola Solutions' financial calendar, as the company has set expectations high by raising its full-year guidance; delivering on that upgraded outlook will be crucial to keeping the share price supported at its current levels.
Motorola Solutions product focus in public safety
Within Motorola Solutions' broad portfolio, a typical public safety deployment combines portable radios such as the APX series with fixed infrastructure, dispatch systems and software that can integrate voice, data and video feeds into a unified command center view. These mission-critical systems are often sold under multi-year contracts to city governments, national agencies or large enterprises, creating long-term customer relationships and steady service revenue streams. The strong 18% year-on-year growth in Software and Services revenue reported for Q1 2026 reflects increasing demand not only for maintenance and support of these systems, but also for newer offerings such as cloud-hosted incident management platforms and video analytics, which can be layered onto existing communications networks.Tormere research As public safety agencies upgrade legacy radio networks and seek to incorporate more advanced analytics and AI-driven features, Motorola Solutions' integrated product and service offering positions it to capture a share of this investment, reinforcing the growth narrative that has underpinned the stock's performance.
Recent trading data compiled in the research source shows that insider sales in August and early September 2026 occurred at prices between approximately USD 469.51 and USD 485.22 per share, indicating that Motorola Solutions stock was trading close to record highs during that period.Tormere research The sale by the CEO on September 2, 2026, at an average price of around USD 485.22 provides a concrete reference level that investors can use to gauge how the current market price compares with the levels at which management chose to take profits.Tormere research For example, the roughly USD 15.71 difference between the lower insider sale price of USD 469.51 and the CEO's USD 485.22 transaction shows how the share price moved upward over a matter of weeks, consistent with the strong Q1 2026 figures and raised guidance that had previously been reported.Tormere research As of the last completed trading day before September 8, 2026, these transactions suggest that Motorola Solutions stock remains in a high valuation band, even though exact real-time quote data are not visible in the available sources.

MSI Gains From Strong Order Bookings: Is Growth Set to Continue?
Motorola Solutions, Inc. MSI is benefiting from strong customer demand. At the end of the second quarter of 2026, backlog reached a record $15.6 billion, up 11% year over year. Software and Services accounted for $11.8 billion, while Products & Systems Integration contributed $3.8 billion.
Products & Systems Integration backlog rose $329 million year over year, supported by strong demand for Mission Critical Networks (MCN) and Video. Software and Services backlog increased $1.2 billion, backed by multiyear contracts across Mission Critical Networks, Video and Command Center.
Management has taken several steps to ensure faster conversion of orders into revenues. Strong LMR demand and accelerated quick-turn conversion, combined with stronger-than-expected device shipments, are expediting revenue growth. Revenues rose 13% year over year to $3.13 billion. MSI registered double-digit growth in both operating segments. Backed by strong order intake, management has raised its 2026 outlook following the strong quarter. The company now expects full-year revenue of approximately $12.975 billion, compared with its previous projection of $12.8 billion. Continued public safety modernization and demand for next-generation safety infrastructure are also expected to drive order bookings in the upcoming quarter. These factors significantly boost MSI's revenue visibility and bring reliability to the company's earnings growth trajectory.
Other Tech Teams With Strong Order Growth

Louisiana public safety contract adds to revenue pipeline

According to Zacks, Motorola Solutions shares trade at 25.49 times forward earnings versus 30.95 times for the broader wireless equipment industry, while the stock has declined 1.7% over the past year against the industry’s 23.4% gain, highlighting both underperformance and potential catch-up room if contract-driven growth feeds through to earnings.

Motorola Solutions last reported quarterly results for the most recent interim period within the past nine months, giving investors an anchor for today’s valuation as management highlighted double-digit revenue growth in mission-critical communications and video security, alongside expanding operating margins in that report.
In that latest quarter, revenue reached a level that represented a mid- to high-single-digit percentage increase over the same period a year earlier, while earnings per share grew at a faster rate thanks to operating leverage and disciplined cost control, reinforcing the thesis that incremental contracts like the Louisiana deal can have a meaningful impact on profitability.

This move into localized cloud infrastructure supports Motorola Solutions’ broader strategy of combining hardware, software and services in integrated safety and security platforms, potentially opening new recurring revenue opportunities and differentiating its offering in markets where data residency and compliance are critical purchase criteria.
For investors, these operational developments provide context for the Louisiana contract and Evercore ISI’s higher price target: both the North American public safety contract and international cloud expansion point to a pipeline of projects that could sustain mid-single-digit to double-digit revenue growth and support the current forward earnings multiple.

A Glimpse at Motorola Solutions Inc's Dividend History
Motorola Solutions Inc has maintained a consistent dividend payment record since 2011, with dividends currently distributed on a quarterly basis. More importantly, the company has increased its dividend each year since 2011. The stock is thus listed as a dividend achiever, an honor given to companies that have raised their dividend each year for at least the past 15 years. This track record reflects management's disciplined commitment to returning capital to shareholders, even through varying economic cycles. For value investors, such consistency often signals financial strength and a shareholder-friendly capital allocation strategy.

Breaking Down Motorola Solutions Inc's Dividend Yield and Growth
As of today, Motorola Solutions Inc currently has a 12-month trailing dividend yield of 1.00% and a 12-month forward dividend yield of 1.02%. The slightly higher forward yield suggests an expectation of increased dividend payments over the next 12 months. While a yield near 1% may appear modest compared to some high-yield sectors, it is important to weigh it against the company's rapid dividend growth and strong share price appreciation, which together have delivered substantial total returns for long-term holders.
Over the past three years, Motorola Solutions Inc's annual dividend growth rate was 11.30%. Extended to a five-year horizon, this rate stayed the same. And over the past decade, Motorola Solutions Inc's annual dividends per share growth rate stands at an impressive 11.60%. This double-digit growth cadence means investors who purchased shares years ago now enjoy a far higher effective yield on their original investment than the current headline yield implies.
Based on Motorola Solutions Inc's dividend yield and five-year growth rate, the 5-year yield on cost of Motorola Solutions Inc stock as of today is approximately 1.71%. Yield on cost measures the annual dividend return relative to an investor's original purchase price, assuming reinvested dividends and historical growth. It illustrates how a steadily rising dividend can compound an investor's income stream over time, even when the current yield looks unremarkable.

The Sustainability Question: Payout Ratio and Profitability
To assess the sustainability of the dividend, one needs to evaluate the company's payout ratio. The dividend payout ratio provides insights into the portion of earnings the company distributes as dividends. A lower ratio suggests that the company retains a significant part of its earnings, thereby ensuring the availability of funds for future growth and unexpected downturns. As of 2026-06-30, Motorola Solutions Inc's dividend payout ratio is 0.29, meaning the company pays out only about 29 cents of every dollar earned. This conservative ratio leaves ample room for continued dividend increases and reinvestment in the business.
Motorola Solutions Inc's profitability rank offers an understanding of the company's earnings prowess relative to its peers. GuruFocus ranks Motorola Solutions Inc's profitability 9 out of 10 as of 2026-06-30, suggesting good profitability prospects. The company has reported net profit in 9 years out of the past 10 years. Strong and consistent profitability is the bedrock of a reliable dividend, and Motorola's track record here reinforces confidence in its ability to sustain and grow future payouts.
To ensure the sustainability of dividends, a company must have robust growth metrics. Motorola Solutions Inc's growth rank of 9 out of 10 suggests that the company's growth trajectory is good relative to its competitors. A high growth rank indicates that the business is expanding its revenue, earnings, and operating cash flow at a healthy pace, which in turn supports the capacity to raise dividends without straining the balance sheet.
Revenue is the lifeblood of any company, and Motorola Solutions Inc's revenue per share, combined with the 3-year revenue growth rate, indicates a strong revenue model. Motorola Solutions Inc's revenue has increased by approximately 9.30% per year on average, a rate that outperforms approximately 74.29% of global competitors. This top-line expansion reflects steady demand for the company's communications and analytics solutions across its government and commercial customer base.
The company's 3-year EPS growth rate showcases its capability to grow its earnings, a critical component for sustaining dividends in the long run. During the past three years, Motorola Solutions Inc's earnings increased by approximately 14.10% per year on average, a rate that outperforms approximately 66.77% of global competitors. Earnings growth that outpaces dividend growth helps keep the payout ratio stable or declining over time.
Lastly, the company's 5-year EBITDA growth rate of 19.20% outperforms approximately 73.32% of global competitors. EBITDA, or earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, is a widely used measure of operating profitability. This strong five-year trend underscores Motorola's ability to convert revenue growth into cash earnings, which ultimately funds both reinvestment and shareholder returns.
Motorola Solutions Inc presents a compelling profile for dividend-focused value investors. The upcoming $1.21 per share payment, payable on 2026-10-15 to shareholders of record before the 2026-09-16 ex-dividend date, continues a streak of annual dividend increases dating back to 2011. With a payout ratio of just 0.29, a profitability rank of 9 out of 10, and double-digit growth in revenue, EPS, and EBITDA, the dividend appears well supported by the underlying business. The modest headline yield of roughly 1% is offset by an 11.60% ten-year dividend growth rate, which has steadily lifted the yield on cost for long-term holders. Investors seeking a growing income stream alongside capital appreciation may find the stock worth monitoring.

Ryan Cohen just put $26 million of his own money into GameStop shares, yet the stock is sliding hard anyway. The question now is whether that insider conviction holds the monthly rally together or profit takers win the argument.
Published September 25, 2026, 10:56am ET · 4 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
The exterior of a GameStop store, symbolizing the company's unexpected financial strength and potential for strategic acquisitions. © GameStop Logo Sign - Vallejo - California (CC BY 2.0) by Will Buckner
Chief executive Ryan Cohen disclosed a $26 million purchase of GameStop (NYSE:GME | GME Price Prediction) shares in a regulatory filing earlier this week, putting his own money behind the retailer at recent levels. GameStop stock is down 8% to $23.11 in morning trading, a drop that still leaves the shares up 29% over the past month.
The VanEck Video Gaming and eSports ETF (NASDAQ:ESPO) is down 0.8%, a much softer dip for a fund that holds GameStop among its gaming names. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 0.11% to $768, leaving the broad market essentially steady. GameStop stock is falling far harder than both funds, which keeps the pressure centered on its own crowded positioning.
Ryan Cohen’s filing showed he bought roughly 1.1 million GameStop shares, and the stock rose once the disclosure became public. That purchase is several sessions old, which means GameStop shares are trading on how holders handle the gain it produced.
The drop in GameStop stock reflects profit taking after that sustained run. Holders who followed Cohen into the shares are booking part of their gains, and the modest declines in the gaming fund and the S&P 500 fund show that selling hasn’t spread beyond this one name.
Within the VanEck fund, GameStop shares made up 4.3% of net assets as of June 30, a mid-sized weighting in a portfolio led by larger game publishers. The rest of the portfolio leans on names such as Capcom, Konami and Bandai Namco, and that mix is posting only a softer decline. That gap shows the selling in GameStop stock is specific to the retailer.
The SPDR fund’s slip is far too small to explain a move of this scale in GameStop shares. Crowded positioning in GameStop stock, built during the monthly run, can amplify an unwind once holders start taking profits, and the stock’s own behavior is carrying the loss.
GameStop’s most recent quarterly profit got a lift from its stake in eBay (NASDAQ:EBAY), a holding of roughly 43.4 million shares valued at $4.9 billion. Earlier this year, GameStop made an unsolicited bid for eBay, which eBay rejected. The retailer has also reduced debt by swapping bonds for company stock, a path that avoided paying out cash. eBay stock is up 0.47% to $108.34.
Weighing Cohen’s Signal Against the Pullback
The optimistic argument for GameStop begins with who bought the shares. A chief executive putting personal money into the shares at recent levels is the least ambiguous signal an insider can send, and the purchase ties Cohen’s fortunes more closely to those of other holders. GameStop also lists its dependence on Ryan Cohen among its risk factors, emphasizing how central he is to the story.
Timing is the problem for GameStop. The stock has given back part of what it gained on the news, so the signal has been priced and then partly reversed. GameStop’s latest quarterly report also flags the concentration of its investment portfolio in eBay common stock as a risk, tying part of the company’s value to a single outside holding.
Whether the monthly gain in GameStop stock holds without a fresh reason to own the shares is what these figures don’t settle. Cohen’s buy, the eBay position and the debt swaps are all known quantities, and none of them is new information. That leaves GameStop shares leaning on sentiment until the company offers its next update.
It is worth watching for any new disclosure from GameStop on its eBay stake or on insider buying, since either could give the shares another reason to move. A second purchase from Cohen would reinforce the original signal, while a quiet stretch could let profit taking run further.
Swings of this magnitude in GameStop stock reward discipline. Anyone adding GameStop shares on the drop ought to stay small, and holders already sitting on gains should size their exposure with that volatility in mind. Setting an exit level in advance can keep a sharp reversal from turning into an oversized hit to their portfolio.
Stocks that fall this hard against a steady market can reverse quickly in either direction. For GameStop, the insider purchase confirms conviction at the top of the company, and the next test for the stock is whether its monthly advance lasts without a new catalyst.

Should You Buy eBay Stock For Its Cash?
Fri, October 2, 2026 at 1:47 AM PDT 4 min read
eBay's (EBAY) free cash flow is 5.2% of its market value, against 4.6% for the median S&P 500 company. A stock usually offers more cash for its price than most for one of two reasons. Investors either underrate the business or expect its cash to shrink. A buyer needs to know whether eBay's cash is underrated or about to shrink.
eBay's free cash flow was $2.4 billion over the last twelve months, up from $1.4 billion a year earlier. Free cash flow is the cash left after a company pays its costs and funds its investment.
As a shareholder, you own a share of that cash whether or not eBay pays it out. Every $10,000 of eBay stock comes with about $520 of free cash flow a year. When investors value that cash more highly, the share price tends to follow. The effect is stronger when the cash is growing.
eBay earns revenue on the sales that pass through its marketplace. The revenue comes from fees, advertising and shipping services. In the second quarter of 2026, eBay kept 14% of the value of goods sold as revenue. The marketplace needs little investment. eBay spent $0.6 billion on capital investment out of the $3.0 billion its operations brought in over the last twelve months.
eBay's free cash flow was positive throughout the last three years, but it did not hold steady. Three years ago it was $2.4 billion, the same as today. It fell to $1.5 billion the following year before recovering.
eBay owes little against that cash. Net debt, which is debt minus cash, was $3.8 billion on its latest reported balance sheet. That debt is 8.1% of eBay's market value. eBay's operating profit is 9.9 times its interest bill.
Why Does eBay Stock Yield More Than Most?
eBay stock yields more partly because the price appears to assume its growth is slowing. The stock lost 7.5% over the past three months, while the S&P 500 returned 2.7%.
Management's own forecast shows a slowdown. Adjusted earnings per share grew 17% in the second quarter of 2026. For the third quarter, management guided growth of 1% to 5%.
On its August 5, 2026 call, management explained the slowdown from the second quarter to the third. Most of it comes from harder comparisons with last year, management said. A year ago, eBay had the benefit of the launch of its U.S. Klarna partnership and of triple-digit growth in Pokémon. Both make comparisons in 2026 tougher.
eBay also bought Depop, a resale business, for $1.4 billion in cash on July 30, 2026. Management expected two effects from Depop in the third quarter. Depop would add about 2.5 points to currency-neutral growth in the value of goods sold. The purchase would also take 3 to 4 points off adjusted operating income growth.
eBay's operating margin, its operating profit per dollar of revenue, has already slipped. The margin was 20.5% over the last twelve months, down from 21.3% a year earlier. Even so, management raised its full-year outlook on the August 5 call. Management also expects Depop to add to adjusted operating income in 2028.
Watch eBay's Earnings Growth Against Its Guide
Adjusted earnings growth above the 1% to 5% that management guided would be a sign that eBay's cash is still rising. Growth at the low end, with a lower operating margin, would be a sign of cash levelling off.
eBay's free cash flow is back at its level of three years ago. The risk is that eBay's cash stops rising as its earnings growth slows.
eBay can carry its debt: its operating profit is 9.9 times its interest bill. The open question is growth. The third-quarter 2026 results will show whether eBay keeps growing through harder comparisons and the cost of Depop.
Does This Mean You Should Act On EBAY?
Our purpose is to inform you with unique data so you make the right investment decisions. That said, betting on a single stock is always risky, no matter which direction you choose.
There is a smarter approach. GameStop Tumbles 8% Despite Ryan Cohen’s $26M Insider Buy; eBay Ticks Up
Ryan Cohen just put $26 million of his own money into GameStop shares, yet the stock is sliding hard anyway. The question now is whether that insider conviction holds the monthly rally together or profit takers win the argument.
Published September 25, 2026, 10:56am ET · 4 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
The exterior of a GameStop store, symbolizing the company's unexpected financial strength and potential for strategic acquisitions. © GameStop Logo Sign - Vallejo - California (CC BY 2.0) by Will Buckner
Chief executive Ryan Cohen disclosed a $26 million purchase of GameStop (NYSE:GME | GME Price Prediction) shares in a regulatory filing earlier this week, putting his own money behind the retailer at recent levels. GameStop stock is down 8% to $23.11 in morning trading, a drop that still leaves the shares up 29% over the past month.
The VanEck Video Gaming and eSports ETF (NASDAQ:ESPO) is down 0.8%, a much softer dip for a fund that holds GameStop among its gaming names. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 0.11% to $768, leaving the broad market essentially steady. GameStop stock is falling far harder than both funds, which keeps the pressure centered on its own crowded positioning.
Ryan Cohen’s filing showed he bought roughly 1.1 million GameStop shares, and the stock rose once the disclosure became public. That purchase is several sessions old, which means GameStop shares are trading on how holders handle the gain it produced.
The drop in GameStop stock reflects profit taking after that sustained run. Holders who followed Cohen into the shares are booking part of their gains, and the modest declines in the gaming fund and the S&P 500 fund show that selling hasn’t spread beyond this one name.
Within the VanEck fund, GameStop shares made up 4.3% of net assets as of June 30, a mid-sized weighting in a portfolio led by larger game publishers. The rest of the portfolio leans on names such as Capcom, Konami and Bandai Namco, and that mix is posting only a softer decline. That gap shows the selling in GameStop stock is specific to the retailer.
The SPDR fund’s slip is far too small to explain a move of this scale in GameStop shares. Crowded positioning in GameStop stock, built during the monthly run, can amplify an unwind once holders start taking profits, and the stock’s own behavior is carrying the loss.
GameStop’s most recent quarterly profit got a lift from its stake in eBay (NASDAQ:EBAY), a holding of roughly 43.4 million shares valued at $4.9 billion. Earlier this year, GameStop made an unsolicited bid for eBay, which eBay rejected. The retailer has also reduced debt by swapping bonds for company stock, a path that avoided paying out cash. eBay stock is up 0.47% to $108.34.
Weighing Cohen’s Signal Against the Pullback
The optimistic argument for GameStop begins with who bought the shares. A chief executive putting personal money into the shares at recent levels is the least ambiguous signal an insider can send, and the purchase ties Cohen’s fortunes more closely to those of other holders. GameStop also lists its dependence on Ryan Cohen among its risk factors, emphasizing how central he is to the story.
Timing is the problem for GameStop. The stock has given back part of what it gained on the news, so the signal has been priced and then partly reversed. GameStop’s latest quarterly report also flags the concentration of its investment portfolio in eBay common stock as a risk, tying part of the company’s value to a single outside holding.
Whether the monthly gain in GameStop stock holds without a fresh reason to own the shares is what these figures don’t settle. Cohen’s buy, the eBay position and the debt swaps are all known quantities, and none of them is new information. That leaves GameStop shares leaning on sentiment until the company offers its next update.
It is worth watching for any new disclosure from GameStop on its eBay stake or on insider buying, since either could give the shares another reason to move. A second purchase from Cohen would reinforce the original signal, while a quiet stretch could let profit taking run further.
Swings of this magnitude in GameStop stock reward discipline. Anyone adding GameStop shares on the drop ought to stay small, and holders already sitting on gains should size their exposure with that volatility in mind. Setting an exit level in advance can keep a sharp reversal from turning into an oversized hit to their portfolio.
Stocks that fall this hard against a steady market can reverse quickly in either direction. For GameStop, the insider purchase confirms conviction at the top of the company, and the next test for the stock is whether its monthly advance lasts without a new catalyst.

Princess Eugenie Apologizes to Meghan Markle Over eBay Fiasco Involving Personal Gift From Duchess
Here's what's being reported about Princess Eugenie's apology to Meghan after her book from duchess was listed on eBay.
Share:
Share on Twitter:
Share on Facebook:
Share via email:
Link copied to the clipboard!
Before she met and started dating Prince Harry, Meghan Markle was friends with his cousin, Princess Eugenie. As the duchess told Oprah Winfrey in her televised interview, “Eugenie and I had known each other before I had known Harry.”
Meghan and Eugenie remained friends when the couple moved across the pond as Eugenie and her husband, Jack Brooksbank, even visited the Sussexes at their Montecito home. So it makes sense that when Meghan published her first children’s book, The Bench, in March 2021, she would send her friend a copy with a personalized note. The only problem is that the book has now ended up on eBay.
Several royal fans noticed the listing for The Bench, and are convinced that it is a personalized copy from the duchess to the princess because the message is in Meghan’s trademark calligraphy-style handwriting.
Message seen inside the book listed on eBay (Image credit: eBay)
It reads, “Dear Eug & Jack, Celebrating the special bond between father and son. I wrote this poem at Frogmore — I hope that Eug, you witness the same love there with your guys. All love, Meghan.”
The listing on eBay has a steep asking price of $26,500. It’s been reported that Eugenie was so “horrified” by the listing that she called Meghan to apologize.
An insider told Rob Shuter’s Naughty But Nice Substack: “Eugenie called Meghan herself. She was horrified the book had somehow ended up for sale and made it absolutely clear she would never knowingly sell a personal gift from Meghan.”
But the mystery is how someone got their hands on it to sell it. That’s not known at this time, or if this copy is even authentic. But many fans took to social media and had a good laugh over it.
“Eugenie listing Meghan’s signed book for 20k is the funniest royal headline in years,” one person wrote, while a second added, “Eugenie probably gave this book away or donated it” with a crying-laughing emoji.
Has a gift from Meghan to Eugenie ended up on eBay? Mystery as 'deeply personal copy of duchess' book The Bench with heartfelt handwritten note to 'Eug and Jack' emerges for sale for £20K https://t.co/BzkYr465L6
— Daily Mail (@DailyMail) October 2, 2026
How Princess Beatrice and Princess Eugenie Disprove Claim Meghan Markle Made During Interview With Oprah
A third posted, “Probably got thrown where it belongs and a staffer picked it up from the bin lol,” and a fourth agreed, writing, “The funniest story would be that Meghan sent the book to Eugenie. Eugenie then gave the book to a staff member bc why would she want it, and then the staff member donated it, and some random person found it in a charity bin and decided to try to resell it. That’s my fan fiction.”
A fifth person commented, “All Meghan’s stuff ends up on eBay” with a crying-laughing emoji.
A sixth exclaimed, “It ended up on eBay. How it ended up there is another question. Either ‘Eug’ put it there herself or her copy was stolen. Or she could have given her copy away to someone else, and that someone else didn’t want it either. Either way, no one wanted to keep it at all, as a personal or family keepsake. 84.4% of Red Ink Comes from These Two Things | The Pitfalls of eBay Exporting
196 items sold, 72.1% profit rate.
Looking at the numbers alone, it seems "going well."
However, the 32 loss-making transactions total -252,021 yen. There was even one item that resulted in a loss of
-61,013 yen.
Could the same hole be hidden behind your "Sold!" notifications?
The moment the joy of "It sold!" freezes over
The most chilling thing about eBay exporting is the moment you realize,
a few days after the sale notification, that your profit calculation is "negative."
"Wait, did I sell this for less than the cost price?"
The "Sold!" text is on your dashboard.
Yet, not a single yen remains in your hand; in fact, money is going out.
This is the reality of "selling at a loss."
I aggregated our sales data for one month and was stunned all over again.
Profit rate (percentage of profitable transactions): 72.1%
These are losses you would never notice if you only looked at the sales figures.
In this article, I have analyzed all 32 loss-making transactions and categorized them into
the 5 major patterns that lead to losses.
84.4% of losses were concentrated in "two causes"
When I classified the 32 loss-making items by cause, this is what I found.
1. Reason not recorded (cases where cause identification was delayed): 18 items / 56.3%
2. Shipping loss (shipping calculation errors/weight miscalculations): 9 items / 28.1%
3. Returns/refund related: 2 items / 6.3%
④ Claim discount handling: 1 case / 3.1%
⑤ Authenticity disputes/cancellations: 2 cases / 6.3%
84.4% of the total (27 cases) are concentrated in ① and ②.
In other words, by just eliminating these two, you can address the majority of your losses.
The biggest minefield is "Audio Equipment"
Looking at it by category, these three had a disproportionately high number of loss cases.
Audio equipment is something people often enter thinking, "It's high-ticket, so it should be easy to make a profit."
In reality, this has become the biggest minefield.
By now, I think you can see the outline of the "structure of losses."
However, what is truly valuable is **"what specifically happened."**
In the following section, I will share:
Actual product names and loss amounts for each of the 5 major categories
A breakdown of the causes for the **worst case (-61,013 yen)**
3 prescriptions you can use starting today
.
If you feel like you might be handling the same products, please continue reading.
If you can prevent just one loss, this article will have more than paid for itself.

Blancco Donates Diagnostics and Data Erasure Software Licenses for Quick Ship’s eBay Live Charity Auction
All auction proceeds directly benefit Jonathan's Landing, a nonprofit that builds neuroinclusive housing and workforce pathways
Boston, MASSACHUSETTS, Sept. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Blancco Technology Group, the industry standard in data erasure and mobile lifecycle solutions, today announced its participation in an eBay Live charity auction initiative led by its customer Quick Ship Brands, a certified reverse logistics, refurbishment, and IT asset disposition company. Blancco donated the diagnostics and certified data erasure software licenses to ensure every donated smartphone, laptop, and desktop could be safely repurposed for the auction.
In an unprecedented effort for the company, Quick Ship donated 100% of the hammer proceeds from electronics they auctioned through eBay Live – a real-time, interactive livestream shopping experience where buyers can bid on and purchase items as they are showcased.
Quick Ship's inaugural charity auction, held on September 16, benefitted Jonathan's Landing Foundation, a 501c3 nonprofit that builds neuroinclusive housing and workforce pathways for adults with autism, intellectual and development disabilities, and other neurodiversities. To date, the charity has raised $150,000 from the auction, including corporate donations and commitments landed after the show.
"We want to thank Blancco for donating the device diagnostic and data erasure software so that each item crossing the screen is verified, sanitized and buyer-ready," said Jordan Insley, founder and CEO of Quick Ship Brands. "We are also thankful for the credentialing organizations CTIA and WISE; they are a key reason a refurbished device carries real trust behind it. And of course, we couldn't serve worthwhile organizations like Jonathan's Landing at this scale without our industry partners. They generously donated valuable inventory that brings value to buyers and supports good, meaningful work."
"It's an honor to collaborate with Jordan and the entire Quick Ship Brands Team on their eBay Live charity initiative," said Blancco Chief Revenue Officer Tom Salah. "We've been fortunate to partner with QuickShip for many years, and it's incredible to see the impact they continue to make. We are proud to support nonprofits like Jonathan's Landing by helping to ensure every donated device undergoes rigorous processing, including testing and data sanitization. Donors can be confident that sensitive data is completely removed before devices are resold, fostering more donations."
For years, Blancco has donated certified data sanitization software licenses to several charities and charity-supporting organizations, including The Turing Trust and Salvation Army Trading Company, among others, to support reuse across four continents. Blancco's regulation-compliant, secure and certified data erasure processes create necessary assurances for device donors, enabling tens of thousands of personal computing devices to be reused to benefit disadvantaged populations.
For information about future charitable auctions, please visit https://quickshipbrands.com/events. To learn more about Blancco's data sanitization and diagnostics solutions, please visit www.blancco.com.
Reduce Risk. Increase Efficiency. Be Sustainable. Blancco Technology Group provides organizations with secure, compliant, and automated solutions that accelerate the transition to the circular economy. Each year, tens of millions of Blancco erasures allow top-tier organizations to protect end-of-life data against unauthorized access, safely redeploy data storage assets, and firmly comply with increased data protection and privacy requirements. Our precise device diagnostics help move used IT assets confidently into the circular economy, enabling enterprises, IT asset disposition (ITAD) vendors and recyclers, and mobile industry stakeholders to operate more sustainably.
Globally approved, recommended, and certified by governing and industry bodies around the world, Blancco is the industry standard in data erasure and mobile lifecycle solutions. With 40+ patented or patent-pending ideas, we continue to grow the number of innovative solutions global companies can rely on to accelerate operations, secure their data, and grow their businesses. Read more about us at blancco.com.
Quick Ship Brands is a certified reverse logistics, refurbishment, and IT asset disposition company with more than 20 years of operating history and two secure U.S. facilities in Glendale, Arizona and Indianapolis, Indiana. The company recovers value from consumer trade-ins, K-12 and enterprise device fleets, big-box retail returns, and brand inventory through one engine: devices are tested and authenticated, erased to NIST SP 800-88 with Blancco-certified reporting, graded, valued against live secondary-market data, and sold per unit across eBay, eBay Live, Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, and its own storefronts. Its proprietary platform, on.xyz, manages serial-level chain of custody, inventory, and analytics across the operation. Quick Ship Brands holds R2v3, ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, OSHA, WISE, and CTIA certifications and has sold more than $1 billion in inventory to date. Learn more at quickshipbrands.com.

Should You Buy eBay Stock For Its Cash?
Fri, October 2, 2026 at 1:47 AM PDT 4 min read
eBay's (EBAY) free cash flow is 5.2% of its market value, against 4.6% for the median S&P 500 company. A stock usually offers more cash for its price than most for one of two reasons. Investors either underrate the business or expect its cash to shrink. A buyer needs to know whether eBay's cash is underrated or about to shrink.
eBay's free cash flow was $2.4 billion over the last twelve months, up from $1.4 billion a year earlier. Free cash flow is the cash left after a company pays its costs and funds its investment.
As a shareholder, you own a share of that cash whether or not eBay pays it out. Every $10,000 of eBay stock comes with about $520 of free cash flow a year. When investors value that cash more highly, the share price tends to follow. The effect is stronger when the cash is growing.
eBay earns revenue on the sales that pass through its marketplace. The revenue comes from fees, advertising and shipping services. In the second quarter of 2026, eBay kept 14% of the value of goods sold as revenue. The marketplace needs little investment. eBay spent $0.6 billion on capital investment out of the $3.0 billion its operations brought in over the last twelve months.
eBay's free cash flow was positive throughout the last three years, but it did not hold steady. Three years ago it was $2.4 billion, the same as today. It fell to $1.5 billion the following year before recovering.
eBay owes little against that cash. Net debt, which is debt minus cash, was $3.8 billion on its latest reported balance sheet. That debt is 8.1% of eBay's market value. eBay's operating profit is 9.9 times its interest bill.
Why Does eBay Stock Yield More Than Most?
eBay stock yields more partly because the price appears to assume its growth is slowing. The stock lost 7.5% over the past three months, while the S&P 500 returned 2.7%.
Management's own forecast shows a slowdown. Adjusted earnings per share grew 17% in the second quarter of 2026. For the third quarter, management guided growth of 1% to 5%.
On its August 5, 2026 call, management explained the slowdown from the second quarter to the third. Most of it comes from harder comparisons with last year, management said. A year ago, eBay had the benefit of the launch of its U.S. Klarna partnership and of triple-digit growth in Pokémon. Both make comparisons in 2026 tougher.
eBay also bought Depop, a resale business, for $1.4 billion in cash on July 30, 2026. Management expected two effects from Depop in the third quarter. Depop would add about 2.5 points to currency-neutral growth in the value of goods sold. The purchase would also take 3 to 4 points off adjusted operating income growth.
eBay's operating margin, its operating profit per dollar of revenue, has already slipped. The margin was 20.5% over the last twelve months, down from 21.3% a year earlier. Even so, management raised its full-year outlook on the August 5 call. Management also expects Depop to add to adjusted operating income in 2028.
Watch eBay's Earnings Growth Against Its Guide
Adjusted earnings growth above the 1% to 5% that management guided would be a sign that eBay's cash is still rising. Growth at the low end, with a lower operating margin, would be a sign of cash levelling off.
eBay's free cash flow is back at its level of three years ago. The risk is that eBay's cash stops rising as its earnings growth slows.
eBay can carry its debt: its operating profit is 9.9 times its interest bill. The open question is growth. The third-quarter 2026 results will show whether eBay keeps growing through harder comparisons and the cost of Depop.
Does This Mean You Should Act On EBAY?
Our purpose is to inform you with unique data so you make the right investment decisions. That said, betting on a single stock is always risky, no matter which direction you choose.
There is a smarter approach. Since its inception, the Trefis High Quality (HQ) Portfolio has returned 105%, beating the benchmark that combines the three major indices - the S&P 500, S&P Mid-cap, and Russell 2000. And it did so without taking the concentrated risk that comes with do-it-yourself stock picking. If that is how you want to invest, the HQ Portfolio is the place to start.

HP’s MacBook Neo Competitor Might Cost You More Than You Think
A colorful shell and pretty screen set the HP OmniBook 5 apart. But make sure to pay attention to the RAM spec.
HP's cheapo laptop is the only one that comes with a colorful, pretty OLED screen. © HP
Apple’s MacBook Neo really kicked all the other laptop makers in the pants earlier this year, and now even HP is trying its hand at a low-cost laptop that doesn’t feel “cheap.” The cheerfully colorful OmniBook 5 packs in a few features no other Neo clone has, but I would still be wary about its price point if I were you.
From the jump, HP wants you to know the OmniBook 5 starts at just $700, the same opening cost of the Apple MacBook Neo. However, that price only accounts for 8GB of LPDDR5-6400 MT/s RAM. If you look on HP’s store page, that’s the only config currently available. Based on my tests with similar laptops, 8GB is not enough to allow for a clean Windows 11 experience. Microsoft is in the process of fixing that, but you shouldn’t buy anything now that provides just the bare hope Windows 11 won’t suck as much in the future.
HP has another configuration with 16GB of RAM, and it says it will launch a version with 12GB sometime in November. A spokesperson for HP told Gizmodo that the 16GB version “is planned” but that the company doesn’t have pricing or availability details to share at this time.
The HP OmniBook 5 comes in Smoke Silver, Starlit Blue, Peony Pink, and Soft Honeydew. © HP
At the very least, the laptop seems light at 2.56 pounds. The MacBook Neo weighs in at 2.7 pounds. The base model also comes with a bare 256GB of storage—same as the MacBook Neo—though you’ll supposedly be able to stretch that to 1TB. The $700 OmniBook 5 model also comes with an Intel Core 5 320 chip, an example from Intel’s Wildcat Lake lineup that has been seen in many low-cost PCs these last few months. You can push the performance with up to an Intel Core 7 350, though that version won’t be around until October.
Let’s take a minute to look at the full arena of MacBook Neo competitors. Dell has two operating at that sub-$1,000 price point, the Dell XPS 13 and Dell 14S. Acer is spinning up a Swift Air 14 with a similar suite of pastel shells. Those laptops are sticking with Intel, but Lenovo is the odd man out with its upcoming IdeaPad Vibe laptops. Those clamshells go even further with vibrant colorways and processor options between an AMD Ryzen AI 400 series chip or a Qualcomm Snapdragon X CPU.
HP is sticking with the same vein of these other brands, simultaneously offering something none of the competition has: an OLED display. Every version of this laptop comes with some variety of organic light-emitting diode screens, which offer a much better sense of contrast than a typical LCD screen. The laptop will launch with options for a touch and non-touch version at 2K resolution (1,920 x 1,200). A 2.5K (2,560 x 1,600) will be along sometime in March 2027. Just know that each screen may not be the brightest of its kind, with a typical luminance of around 300 nits, according to HP’s specs page.
There’s a lot to like here, but I can’t help but feel downtrodden. MacBooks can get away with 8GB of unified memory because—well—macOS is simply better designed for lower memory configurations than Windows 11.
